title: Consolidate golden-signal ingestion for token SLIs and build multi-region load-shed simulation dashboard
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: We currently have fragmented token-level latency and error telemetry across tracing, sampling pipelines, and ad-hoc dashboards. That makes it hard to reason about SLO regressions during multi-region failover or when circuit breakers trigger. This ticket consolidates a single golden-signal ingestion path for per-token SLIs, standardizes SLI derivations, and delivers a simulation dashboard for multi-region failover and adaptive load-shed tuning.
goals: Create a normalized token-level golden-signal stream (latency, errors, admittance, kv-hit) for downstream SLI derivations
Define canonical per-token SLI derivations (p50/p95/p99 tail, error-rate by token class, admit ratio) and surface them in metrics store
Ship a dashboard that simulates multi-region failover scenarios with synthetic traffic replay and shows circuit state, shed actions, and SLO impact over time
Produce an operational playbook: threshold recommendations, hysteresis settings, and rollback steps for adaptive shedding and circuit breakers
acceptance_criteria: Normalized token telemetry is available in metrics backend (Prometheus/Tracing bridge) with stable metric names
Canonical SLI queries documented and validated against production sampling data
Simulation dashboard contains: region-level admit rates, per-token latency percentiles, KV cache hit-rate, circuit states, and simulated traffic replay controls
Playbook published in Confluence with run steps, example alert thresholds, and post-incident checklist
Load-shed thresholds validated via canary replay that shows <5% false-positive sheds on baseline traffic and measurable SLO improvement under overload
tasks: Design normalized schema for token-level golden signals (fields, cardinality limits)
Implement lightweight agent to enrich trace spans with token_class and kv_hit annotations
Add metric exporter to summarize spans into metrics (token_latency_ms_bucket, token_errors_total, token_admit_ratio)
Author canonical SLI PromQL/SQL derivations and store in repo
Build Grafana dashboard panels for multi-region failover simulation and sequence waterfall visualization
Integrate synthetic traffic harness (replay recorded traces) into staging clusters across regions
Run chaos experiments (region outage, high qps spike) and iterate on hysteresis tuning
Write playbook with threshold guidance and incident runbook steps
notes: Cardinality: tokens are high-cardinality; we will collapse to token_class (e.g., short_prompt, long_prompt, embeddings, rerank) at ingestion to keep metric cardinality tractable
Sampling: full-token telemetry retained for short windows; metrics computed from sampled spans to bound cost
KV cache: add a boolean kv_prefetch and enum kv_status (hit|miss|stale) to traces to enable KV-impact panels
Circuit state: wire circuit manager events into metrics (circuit_opened{region,shard}, circuit_closed, shed_action) for dashboard timeline
Failover sim: reuse existing synthetic harness from ENG-48888 but augment with multi-region routing and token-class skewing
queries_examples: token_latency_p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, token_class, region))
token_error_rate: sum(rate(token_errors_total[5m])) by (token_class, region) / sum(rate(token_requests_total[5m])) by (token_class, region)
kv_hit_rate: sum(rate(token_kv_hit_total[5m])) by (region, token_class) / sum(rate(token_kv_lookup_total[5m])) by (region, token_class)
implementation_decisions: Use token_class bucketing to reduce cardinality and map back to detailed sampling for forensic queries
Compute percentile rollups in metrics pipeline (Prometheus bucket histograms) rather than raw span aggregation to improve dashboard performance
Expose a small set of 'control knobs' on dashboard: inject_region_latency, traffic_multiplier, token_class_mix to drive replay
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: metric cardinality explosion -> Mitigation: token_class bucketing + sample-based detailed tracing
Risk: false-positive shedding during tests -> Mitigation: conservative hysteresis and A/B canaries with labeled synthetic traffic
Risk: storage/cost spike for high-resolution histograms -> Mitigation: downsample long-term aggregates and keep high-res only for 24-72h
testing_plan: Unit tests for exporter and schema validation
Staging rollout with synthetic replay across 3 regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west)
Controlled chaos tests: regional partition, KV store latency injection, kernel slowdown
Canary in prod: enable tokens SLI metric export for 10% of traffic and compare against sampled traces
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement exporter + dashboard in staging, exercise replay harness
Phase 2 (canary): enable metrics export for low-traffic orgs in dedicated cluster; validate SLI derivations
Phase 3 (gradual): increase export to 25% then 100% with cost monitoring and retention tuning
Phase 4 (GA): publish playbook and onboard on-call rotations to new dashboard alerts
